newsitem.title: UK: Holed gasoline tanker leaves for Rotterdam.
newsitem.headline: Holed gasoline tanker leaves for Rotterdam.

text.p: The holed tanker Bona Fulmar, which leaked some 7,000 tonnes of gasoline into the Channel following a collision, is en route to Rotterdam after temporary repairs, a spokesman for the vessel's managers said on Monday.
Asked if any ships had been delayed or diverted by the accident, the spokesman for Oslo-based Bona Shipping said: "No."
Spokesman Roger Kornberg said he believed the gasoline was quickly evaporating and would not pose a serious pollution threat.
"She will discharge the rest of her cargo on Rotterdam," he added.

He said the 78,585 dwt Bahamian-flagged vessel was proceeding under its own power to Rotterdam but was being accompanied by a tug as a precaution. Its hull was damaged below the waterline and one cargo tank was ruptured.
None of the 26 crew and two passengers on board was injured when the Bona Fulmar was in collision with a Mexican chemical tanker, the Teoatl, on Saturday.
The combination carrier was carrying 58,447 tonnes of unleaded gasoline from Antwerp to New York when the accident occurred northwest of Dunkirk, Bona Shipping said. The Teoatl was not damaged.
The Bona Fulmar was under charter to U.S. trader George E. Warren, shipbrokers said.
